cases.note:
C1 attack: trailing '
' must be rejected by _VERSION_RE.fullmatch (selection.py:50,77). An implementation built on re.match+$ would silently accept '1.21.0
'; the 
 would then also be dropped by Java-side parsing, so only fullmatch preserves the strict contract. Base file is present so a buggy accept path would return base_only, not error.
CRLF line ending on the request string: same fullmatch gate; '$'-style matching tolerates a single trailing newline only, so \r\n is caught even by weaker implementations, but must be pinned anyway.
Two well-formed versions separated by a newline. Rejects any impl that strips whitespace or takes the first/last line; neither 1.21.0 nor 1.22.0 may be selected.
ASCII space is outside the component grammar; also covers any impl that calls str.strip() before matching (contract forbids silent normalization — request_raw must equal the CLI string).

C1 attack: U+FF15 FULLWIDTH DIGIT FIVE is Unicode category Nd. [0-9] (selection.py:50) rejects it; a \d-based regex would match AND Python int('５')==5 would normalize the request to 1.21.5 — the planted exact diff makes that buggy path produce exact_diff, a silent wrong-success rather than a rejection. Canonical-decimal contract requires ASCII digits only.

Whole-version substitution with Arabic-Indic digits (U+0661 U+0662 U+0661 . U+0660): Nd-category digits that int() would accept ('١٢١'->121). Java Integer.parseInt also accepts them, so the strict contract is deliberately tighter than source here; rejection pins the model's ASCII-only grammar.

Mixed ASCII + U+1D7D9 MATHEMATICAL DOUBLE-STRUCK DIGIT ONE inside the minor component. Plane-1 Nd digit: catches implementations that assume non-ASCII means BMP-only or that accept any Unicode decimal.

C1 attack: major = Integer.MAX_VALUE+1. 10 digits so it passes the length guard (selection.py:83-88) and must be caught by the range check (:90-94). Java Integer.parseInt would throw NumberFormatException; strict model maps to RequestError/exit2.
Minor component at int max+1: same range check must fire per-component, not only on major.
Patch component at int max+1: also guards against an impl that bounds patch by the diff directory scan and skips range validation entirely.

11-digit component: exercises the pre-int() length guard (selection.py:83-88) rather than the numeric compare — without it, int() on huge digit strings raises plain ValueError past Python's ~4300-digit limit, which is NOT RequestError and would escape the CLI's exit-2 typed-error path as an unhandled traceback.

0.0.* matches the M.m.p regex and each component is in range, so rejection must come from the (0,0,*) INVALID-sentinel check (selection.py:95-99, GoVer.isInvalid). Planted go0.0.0.json means a buggy accept returns base_only — a wrong-success, not a wrong-error.

Empty GOOS: arch_search_order (selection.py:104-105) must reject before any filesystem lookup. An impl that skipped validation would emit order ['-amd64','','amd64','all'] and quietly return missing_base.
Empty GOARCH: same selector-validation path, symmetric coverage.

Valid int-max patch on an installed minor: Java's getPatchVerDiffFile counts DOWN from patch (GoApiSnapshot.java:150-157) so 2^31-1 is a legal request that lands on the highest present diff. Installed 12.1.4 listing tops out at go1.24.6.json.diff — this fixture's tree mirrors that bound and expects fallback_diff/selected_patch=6, exactly what the installed root would produce.

Every component exactly at Integer.MAX_VALUE: must parse (boundary is inclusive — off-by-one '<' vs '<=' in the range check would wrongly reject), then yield missing_base. Bounded by the installed listing: Ghidra 12.1.4 ships go1.15.0..go1.25.0 only, so no int-max base exists on the real root either.

Calibration: major==0 with nonzero minor is NOT the INVALID sentinel (GoVer.isInvalid checks major==0 && minor==0, selection.py:95). An over-broad 'reject major 0' impl would wrongly RequestError this legal request.

Non-ASCII digit in a diff FILENAME (go1.21.５.json.diff, fullwidth 5): _DIFF_NAME_RE.fullmatch (selection.py:55-56,216) must not match, so the entry is skipped and the result is base_only/selected_patch=0 — Java builds the candidate name from canonical GoVer.toString() and would never spell it this way either.

Leading-zero patch in a diff filename must not alias patch 5: canonical GoVer.toString() never emits leading zeros, so the scan skips it. A naive r'go(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)' scan + int() would treat '05' as 5 and wrongly select exact_diff.

goos==goarch produces 'linux' twice in the emitted order (selection.py:109-115 emits duplicates; :243-249 dedups only for bucket membership). Source-faithful: Java List.of at GoApiSnapshot.java:109-110 retains duplicate elements (only Set.of/Map.of reject them; JDK21 ImmutableCollections.listFromTrustedArray null-checks only) and read() iterates the list with a Set membership test (GoApiSnapshot.java:228-237), so the emitted list itself carries the dup and matching dedups — exactly what this case pins.
